references_named: Michelangelo Buonarroti, the Prigioni / non-finito (Atlas, Bearded, Awakening Slaves, c. 1520-34)
the web 'read more' / line-clamp truncation pattern
rationale: All six gates pass. The mechanism (CSS text-overflow:ellipsis + nowrap + overflow:hidden) is materially distinct from the catalogued source-vs-render works (Silencio uses white-space, La Disparition uses beforeinput, Indivisible uses hyphens:auto, Scrittura Speculare uses scaleX(-1)) and the reference (Michelangelo's non-finito) is fresh. The truncation literally enacts the carving (P1) — the layout engine's job IS deciding how much text a box may reveal, and the U+2026 glyph lives only in the render, invisible to textContent and dropped on copy, which is a precise and web-specific observation. The self-referential sentences get cut by the very mechanism they describe, a clean P7/P9 double-coding move. Restraint is strong (P3): six lines, one CSS property doing the sculpting, a single rAF-bound resize handler.
reservations: The source-vs-render family in the catalogue is now five works deep (Silencio, La Disparition, Indivisible, Scrittura Speculare, Non-finito); the argument risks becoming a local tic. Novelty is the weakest axis because the broader gesture is already established, even though this specific mechanism and reference are new. The 'marble' gradient background is mildly illustrative — a risk of drifting toward decoration, though it is restrained enough to pass.
revision_suggestion: If the source-vs-render family needs pruning in the catalogue, this work could be reframed to put equal weight on the Michelangelo / 'always inside the stone' argument and less on the source-vs-render meta-point, so it reads as the non-finito thesis first and as a sibling to Silencio second.
